To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the absorbance of biological samples stored in microcentrifuge plastic tubes is affected by chemicals that leach from the tube material.

normal handling of plastic microtubes causes release of chemicals into biological samples and that these chemicals interfere with spectrophotrmetric analyses of nucleic acids, proteins, and other biomolecules.
leaching of chemicals into solutions stored in plastic tubes causes errors in the quantitation and detection of nucleic acids, proteins, and other biomolecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the leaching of chemicals into aqueous solutions from plastic microtubes used to store and manipulate biological samples.
the effects of leaching on absorbance measurements.
the leaching of chemicals out of microtubes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the absorbance spectra of aqueous solutions in plastic microcentrifuge (or other) tubes should be measured prior to any use in order to determine the magnitude of any absorbance at the wavelengths of interest.

leaching of chemicals into solutions stored in plastic laboratory microtubes is a significant source of error in spectrophotometric detection and quantitation of nucleic acids, proteins, and other biomolecules.
the absorbance spectroscopy of nucleic acids or proteins is not reliable if they are handled or stored in plastic tubes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
absorbance measurements at 220 and at 260 nm should be performed with extreme caution, and preferably in quartz cuvettes.
absorbance spectroscopy is an excellent method for monitoring the concentrations of nucleosides, nucleotides, nucleic acids, and proteins in aqueous solution.
the absorbance spectra obtained from solutions in polypropylene microtubes should be considered suspect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of leached plastic additives should be considered in any spectrophotometric assay that uses plastic tubes.
the use of plastic microtubes to manipulate and store biological solutions can lead to significant overestimation of protein and DNA concentrations.
the absorbance spectra of biological samples stored in plastic tubes should be compared to those of the same solutions stored in tubes made of a non-plastic material.
